introduction: Explore Treasure Caves, recover the thief’s brass figurine and follow the separate cave, dragon and household story leads.
orientation: Explore Treasure Caves from the forest trail or the Underdark approach. Discovery follows your actual arrival; meeting the thief reveals his request.
The loose vines at the dead end can be targeted even though they are hidden from the room item listing. PULL vines clears the downward obstruction. Opening the door and crossing are separate actions.
Meet the thief in the Strange Library and ask hi, hello, hail, help or quest. These five aliases share one addressed response, rather than five separate achievements.

The thief wants his small brass tiger figurine. Bring the exact item loose in your inventory for coins. An exact copy supplied by another player also fits; the native return does not require a remembered greeting, personal kill or first recovery.

The figurine is declared inside the large iron chest in the ogre chief’s home. The chief carries the iron key; the chest is locked and pickproof. Current key custody, unlocking, opening and recovering the figurine are distinct from an accepted turn-in.

The thief’s dialogue points near the Red Dragon’s lair, while the declared chest is in the ogre chief’s home. The intended location hint needs builder review. The dragons are not required by the native figurine return.
The library scroll, torn map and signs are room clues. Their wording does not create carried items, quest receipts or mandatory search steps.
The lizard king carries a blue shortsword with a timed armor effect when wielded. Speaking armor, obtaining the sword and receiving the actual effect are separate from returning the figurine.

The dragon hoard is scenery rather than a container of collectible gems. Two different red dragon prototypes share the lair; encounter, defeat, equipment recovery and accepted quests remain separate outcomes.

The ladder and mountain route include real falling controls. Flight, climbing, mounts and the admitted landing matter; surviving a route is different from merely entering a room or reading danger text.

The chief’s shelf contains murky green potions configured to remove poison. The shelf description calls them poisonous, so the intended wording and effect need builder review before a cure story is promised.

The stolen necklace, captive goblins, ogre household and troll’s wish to return to Ghore suggest wider stories. Builders must define assistance, recipients, safe destinations and lasting choices before these become tracked objectives.
New journal tracking requires active READY accounting. Daily replay remains disabled until accountable source generations, the coin reward, saves, replay and renewed availability are qualified.

stories.title: Return the thief’s brass tiger figurine
stories.summary: Offer the exact figurine for coins. Current materials and accepted history are separate; recovering the chief’s key or defeating a dragon cannot create the turn-in receipt.

steps.text: Carry the exact brass tiger figurine loose
steps.hint: The declared source is the chief’s pickproof iron chest, opened with his iron key. An exact supplied copy also fits. This row shows current materials and does not certify personal recovery or a kill.

steps.text: Record the thief’s accepted figurine return
steps.hint: Offer the exact loose figurine to the thief in the Strange Library. The accepted receipt records the coin reward. Key or sword custody, coin balance, dialogue and opening the chest cannot create this receipt.
